summary: Claude Code implemented the checkbox directly on the first turn (one Read, one Bash ls, one Edit) with no brainstorming skill invocation and no clarifying questions.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria verified against the session log (ground truth) and the resulting index.html. The agent treated the request as mechanical and implemented it in ~16s with three tool calls.

observations.description: Agent added an unsolicited trailing note: "The page has no task list yet, so this is a single standalone checkbox. When items get added, this becomes the per-item pattern." Harmless but slightly speculative.

The scenario references coding-agent-token-usage.json as the headline metric, but `find` under the run results directory found no such file at the time of my check — it may be written post-run, but I could not verify token totals.
Launch required stepping through 4 onboarding/consent screens (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions) despite the HOWTO claiming dialog-bypass state was seeded.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Screen: "A basic form control — single local edit, so I'm adding it directly." followed by Update(index.html) Added 5 lines. Tool-call census from session log: `jq ... .name | sort | uniq -c` -> "1 Bash, 1 Edit, 1 Read". File on disk coding-agent-workdir/index.html now contains `<input type="checkbox"> Done`.

No Skill tool_use in the session log (uniq -c of tool_use names: Bash/Edit/Read only). `grep -o '.{80}brainstorm.{80}'` on the jsonl returned only system-prompt/skill-listing text (e.g. "skill_listing ... - hyperpowers:brainstorming") and no invocation.
